ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP and sanctions screening under Canadian AML/CFT doctrine applied to this PropTech SaaS issuer (standard-risk tier, payments via licensed PSPs): (1) screen every director, officer, and individual with significant control (CBCA s. 21.1, threshold 25%) against Global Affairs Canada Consolidated Sanctions List (Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act), UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list (compulsory exposure because of USD-denominated ACH rails), and domestic anti-money-laundering watchlists; (2) on any domestic or foreign PEP, head of an international organization, or their family member/close associate (Criminal Code s. 462.3), apply enhanced due diligence including independent asset and wealth-source corroboration; (3) complete sanctions-hit screening documentation with search date and database snapshot, archived in the corporate CIP file; (4) retain AML/CFT records for at least five years post-relationship per PCMLTFA s. 72; (5) re-screen monthly during pre-incorporation and upon every share issuance or control change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) - Online Filing Centre at corporationscanada.ic.gc.ca, including the NUANS name search request module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under CBCA s. 10 and Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001 (SOR/2001-512) ss. 5-7, the corporate name must be stated in English, French, or both, and must contain a mandatory legal element: Limited, Limitée, Incorporated, Incorporée, Corporation, Société par actions, or the abbreviations Ltd., Ltée, Inc., Corp., S.A. There is no transliteration doctrine for Latin-script names; names submitted in non-Latin scripts must include a Latin-script transliteration or translation to permit NUANS similarity screening against federal, provincial, and registered trademark names. Accented French characters are permitted. The name must be distinctive and not deceptive or confusing within the meaning of the CBCA distinguishing test.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Trust Company, Insurance, Assurance, Reinsurance (require prior OSFI approval under federal financial statutes)
Canada, Federal, Crown, Royal, Queen, Prince, Princess, Governor General, Parliament, Senate, Privy Council (suggest Crown connection; require Governor in Council or Director permission)
RCMP, Police, Municipal, Regional (law-enforcement connotation; ministerial or gazetted approval required)
University, College, Polytechnic, Institute (provincial educational authority approval required)
Engineer, Professional Engineer, Architect, Geoscientist, Physician, Surgeon, Lawyer, Barrister, Notary, Accountant, Auditor (regulated professions; holding of underlying licence required)
Olympic, Red Cross, United Nations, World Trade Organization, NATO (statutorily protected marks or misleading connotation)
Real Estate Broker, Mortgage Lender, Property Manager, Tenant Screening Bureau (deceptively misdescriptive unless the corporation holds or will hold the applicable provincial licence)
Words that are obscene, scandalous, or contrary to public order, or that imply connection with a government program
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On name refusal: (1) request written reasons from Corporations Canada; (2) within 30 days, submit a reconsideration letter to the Director, Corporations Canada (CBCA s. 11(1)-(2)) with rebuttal NUANS evidence and, if applicable, trademark coexistence consent letters; (3) concurrently reserve up to three substitute names, each NUANS-backed and valid for 90 days; (4) request an extension of an existing reservation before expiry under CBCA s. 10.1(2)(b) if material commercial steps remain outstanding; (5) if the Director reaffirms refusal, seek judicial review in the Federal Court of Canada within 30 days under CBCA s. 11(2) and Federal Courts Act s. 18.1, the court applying the deceptively similar standard of CBCA s. 10(2); typical judicial-review legal costs range CAD 5,000-15,000.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with conditions. CBCA s. 19 requires the registered office to be located in Canada at a physical street address accessible to the public during normal business hours for service of process and statutory records inspection. A commercial virtual office providing a physical street address, mail handling, and standard-hours reception is accepted for this standard-risk PropTech / real-estate SaaS business, provided it is not a bare post-office box. The entity must keep its books and records (articles, by-laws, shareholder register, ISC register) at that location or otherwise permit inspection there, and must disclose a separate real operating address to the CRA for GST/HST and income-tax purposes. Non-resident ownership is unrestricted, but CBCA s. 105(3) requires a majority of resident Canadian directors; failure to maintain this blocks corporate filings and exposes the corporation to dissolution proceedings by the Director.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated 1-3% probability of an unannounced physical inspection in the first 12 months. Federal registry oversight under the CBCA is records-based; CRA income-tax and GST/HST audits are normally announced in advance; FINTRAC/MSB on-site examination risk does not apply because Stripe Billing and ACH payment rails are operated by licensed third-party payment service providers and the corporation is not a money services business. A records demand (rather than physical inspection) is moderately expected at 10-15% in year one.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C., 1985, c. C-44, as amended; principal sections: s. 8 (Articles of Incorporation), s. 9 (Certificate of Incorporation), s. 19 (registered office), s. 104 (first directors), s. 106 (by-laws), s. 114 (officers), ss. 124-126 (written resolutions and share subscriptions), s. 128 (share certificates); supplemented by the Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001 (SOR/2001-512).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) - Federal Incorporation Division
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 4001) filed together with Initial Notice of Directors (Form 4006) and registered office particulars; issuance instrument: Certificate of Incorporation under CBCA s. 9.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital exists under the CBCA; the Corporation may validly incorporate with one or more common shares of nominal or par value. Federal law imposes no escrow account or capital deposit requirement for a private business corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. The subscriptions for the common shares set forth in the subscription schedule annexed hereto are accepted, and share certificates shall be issued upon full payment of the subscription price. 2. The registered office of the Corporation be and is hereby established at [street address, city, province, postal code], Canada, which premises are open for statutory service of process, and the Corporate Secretary shall file the required notice with Corporations Canada. 3. The corporate by-laws submitted to this meeting are approved and adopted as the governance documents of the Corporation. 4. [Name of CEO] is appointed Chief Executive Officer and [Name of Corporate Secretary] is appointed Corporate Secretary, each vested with the authority of their respective offices. CARRIED.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Selection and NUANS Pre-Clearance (Optional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada (NUANS search system administered under ISED policy)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a licensed NUANS search provider to run a preliminary Canadian trademark and corporate name search using the proposed corporate name; review the Name Search Report against prohibited marks and confusing names; either reserve the approved name for continued use or decide to incorporate as an unnamed numbered corporation (e.g., 1234567 Canada Inc.).
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and two alternate names
Completed NUANS search request via accredited provider
Name compliance checklist under Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001
Authority documents for the filing agent (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NUANS report shows a confusingly similar name or the Director of Corporations refuses the name, re-run the search on an alternate name or elect a numbered company; no filing fee is lost because the incorporation fee is payable at submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Articles and Statutory Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada - Federal Incorporation online filing questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Articles of Incorporation (Form 4001) containing the corporate name or numbered designation, registered office province, share structure and share class rights, any restrictions on transfers, number of directors, and first directors; complete Form 4006 Initial Notice of Directors with each director's name, residential address, and signed or digitally attested consent; verify registered office jurisdiction and confirm the office is at a fixed address in Canada.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (Form 4001) - completed
Initial Notice of Directors (Form 4006)
Registered office information
Consent to act as director for each initial director
NUANS Name Search Report (only for named corporations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Corporations Canada may issue a Notice of Deficiency requesting corrected information; amend the defective fields and refile within the stated statutory period (normally 30 days); if the registered office province is inconsistent with the provincial registry rules, select the correct province and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission, Fee Payment, and Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada online portal (strategis.ic.gc.ca / federal incorporation service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create an account on Corporations Canada's online filing system, transcribe the validated articles and director data into the e-filing questionnaire, authenticate the submittal, and pay the application fee online by credit card (CAD 200 for online filings; CAD 250 for paper); the system issues the Certificate of Incorporation within minutes; effect of incorporation takes effect on the date shown in the certificate.
required_dossiers: Completed Corporations Canada e-filing questionnaire
Scanned/signed Articles of Incorporation, if required by portal
Director information and consents
Credit card or electronic payment mechanism
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected (technical or document error), correct the portal comments and re-submit; if the certificate shows an error, apply to Corporations Canada for an amendment under CBCA s. 260 or address a clerical error via a letter of correction; fees are refunded only where no certificate is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Organization and Corporate Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation - registered office and corporate secretary (private governance, not a government filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of directors or pass written resolutions pursuant to CBCA s. 117; adopt By-law No. 1 (general corporate governance); accept the subscriptions for shares, authorize share issuance, and enter all matters in the minute book; establish the securities register, directors register, and officers register; issue share certificates in compliance with CBCA s. 49 (restrictions) and s. 128.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Draft By-law No. 1
Subscription agreements and share certificate stubs
Organizational written resolutions
Minute book, corporate seal, and statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any missing signatures or consents by retroactive resolution passed by all directors; if shares are issued for non-cash consideration, file the required CBCA declaration as to consideration and record it in the register within the prescribed time.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Business Number Registration and Initial Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online (BRO) portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Corporation for its nine-digit Business Number (BN) via the CRA's Business Registration Online service using the federal incorporation number; open required program accounts: corporate income tax account, GST/HST account if annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 (or voluntarily), payroll account if employees are hired, and any import/export accounts as needed; complete and retain CRA Form RC1 evidence.
required_dossiers: Federal incorporation number and Certificate of Incorporation
Corporation legal name and registered office address
Directors' and officers' contact information
Estimated revenue thresholds for GST/HST and payroll obligations
Business banking details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA sends a verification letter or flags incomplete data, log into the CRA Represent a Client portal or call Business Enquiries to update the profile; if a program account (e.g., GST/HST) was not opened, file a late election or register retroactively under the Excise Tax Act and settle any associated filing obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - ISIC 6201 (computer programming / cloud software) attracts no federal industrial operating license in Canada; the Corporation's physical component is limited to administrative office premises, which require a municipal business license from the local municipality (e.g., City of Toronto) rather than an industry licensing board.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no statutory federal operating or manufacturing permit exists for the Corporation's PropTech SaaS activity; voluntary municipal business license and compliance with the federal Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA) apply as the entity commences operations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 (CEPA 1999) and the Impact Assessment Act (IAA), S.C. 2019, c. 28
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the Corporation performs no physical construction, manufacturing, or resource activity; cloud-based software services are below any trigger threshold for an IAA designation, so no full environmental impact assessment report or registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to software operations: no wastewater, VOC emissions, regulated air pollutants, or hazardous waste streams are generated; standard office waste streams and e-waste are handled under provincial/territorial municipal waste and electronics recycling rules; data centre energy use is outside the Corporation's ownership boundary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office premises must comply with the National Fire Code of Canada 2020 and applicable provincial building and fire codes, with fire safety certification obtained from the local fire marshal; workplace clearance under the applicable provincial occupational health and safety statute (e.g., Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1990 for Ontario), including first-aid and fire-extinguisher provisions; no structural load inspection applies to standard Class A or Class B office tenancies beyond municipal building permits.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); online portal: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-business-portal.html); GST/HST NETFILE; Business Registration Online (BRO) via canada.ca
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign corporations must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account. Steps: (1) Apply via Business Registration Online (BRO) or complete Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts); (2) designate a person resident in Canada or rely on a qualified non-resident representative; (3) provide corporate charter, certified copy of articles of incorporation (foreign entity), director IDs, address for service in Canada; (4) CRA issues a 9-digit BN plus program account suffix (e.g., RT0001 for GST/HST); (5) register for non-resident simplified GST/HST if supplying digital services (including SaaS) to Canadian residents and taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000; (6) open a payroll account (RP) if hiring Canadian employees; not required for pure B2B SaaS without payroll. Registration is mandatory before invoicing Canadian clients subject to GST/HST.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box regime. A Canadian federal corporation is by default a resident taxable corporation under Part I of the Income Tax Act. Key elections: (a) Section 216(1) election to return Canadian real property net rental income on a net basis (for non-resident corporations); (b) Section 89 election re paid-up capital and safe income; (c) Specified corporate partnership loss restriction no election; (d) GST/HST Quick Method election (S. 172 ETA) - simplified net tax calculation for small businesses; (e) GST/HST related-person election under S. 156 ETA to net settlements; (f) Financial institution segregation election; (g) Hybrid mismatch rules (S. 18.4, 18.5 ITA) - no election, mandatory anti-avoidance; (h) A 'check-the-box' style election to treat a Canadian subsidiary as a branch of a US parent is NOT available under Canadian law; treaty-based dual-resident tie-breaker applies via competent authority (MAP).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), operating concurrently with the Department of Finance Canada; FX policy is administered under the Currency Act and operates in a liberalized environment with no exchange-control board. Bank and clearing supervision is delegated to the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), the Canadian Payments Act administrator, and FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible and Canada maintains unrestricted current-account and capital-account convertibility; there is no exchange-control approval, no investment licensing, and no profit-repatriation permit for ISIC 6201 (PropTech SaaS). Dividends, royalties, management fees, and interest may be remitted freely, subject only to Part XIII withholding tax (statutory 25%; reduced by treaty, e.g., 5-15% for US-dividend recipients, 10% royalties, 0-15% interest). Inward equity investment is unrestricted for non-residents and no minimum-capital or escrow requirement applies to a CBCA Business Corporation; only a post-incorporation notice under the Investment Canada Act is required. The platform's foreign-produced subscription revenue is not subject to export-surrender constraints and may be consolidated in CAD or USD accounts at Canadian banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender, mandatory conversion, or repatriation timeline exists in Canada; the Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951. Foreign-currency receivables from overseas SaaS and tenant-screening clients may be settled via FX conversion at commercial rates, held in USD accounts, or netted offshore without reporting to the central bank, provided transactions are reflected in the CRA tax filings and are subject to FINTRAC electronic-funds-transfer reporting (threshold CAD 10,000) when cleared through a Canadian bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD/USD multi-currency) with FX forward and Lynx settlement
Operational Account (CAD/USD) with foreign-ownership desk and treasury services
Operational Account; Capital Escrow Account through Scotiatrust
Operational Account with cross-border US/Canada integrated cash repositioning

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Low-as-primary / High-as-auxiliary. Canada does not issue EU-style EMI licences; non-resident digital banks (Wise Business, Payoneer, Airwallex) operate as Money Service Businesses (MSB) or payment-service providers registered with FINTRAC and, since November 2024, with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act. Such PSPs are legally usable for collecting subscription fees through Stripe Billing or for small-value disbursements, but they cannot maintain a Lynx settlement account, cannot hold the corporate payroll/tax float, and cannot execute deliverable FX forwards on behalf of a CBCA entity. The entity should use a Schedule I D-SIB account as the primary source-of-funds treasury and restrict EMIs to daily operational float below CAD 50,000.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is conditionally permitted. Schedule I banks accept CBCA federal corporations via video-KYC where the authorized signatory is identity-verified, the registered office and principal place of business are evidenced by lease or utility record, and the Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register is disclosed. A physical in-person interview at a Canadian branch is normally waived for Low_Risk_Standard PropTech entities when all directors are from recognized low-risk jurisdictions (US, EU, UK, CA); if any material UBO resides in a FATF grey-listed country, a physical interview or correspondent-bank proof is mandated, extending onboarding to 4-8 weeks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO with 25% or greater control appearing only in the CBCA register without source-of-wealth documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBCA Articles of Incorporation, ISC Register, certified passport copies, group ownership chart, sworn source-of-wealth declaration supported by foreign bank statements and audited financial statements of the shareholder for the capital-injection period.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital originated from an offshore jurisdiction (Cayman, BVI, or grey-listed state) or routed through a third-party payment intermediary
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete SWIFT MT103 chain maintained by the account-holding bank, twelve-month intermediary bank statements, annotated share subscription agreement, tax-residency certificate of the sender, and a Legal-Source-of-Funds memorandum prepared by external counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Misclassification of PropTech scope when platform ledger shows tenant rental-payment flows alongside SaaS fees, creating unlicensed money-services exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed software-as-a-service master agreements, tenant-screening service descriptions, written confirmation from external counsel that the entity is not handling funds in the capacity of money services business, FINTRAC no-registration confirmation or MSB registration if deposit-taking emerges, and PIPEDA privacy-impact assessment for rental-screening data.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Provincial footprint mismatch: operation in Ontario, British Columbia, and Quebec without extra-provincial registration causes account-ownership ambiguity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Articles of extra-provincial registration for each operating province, CRA Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account confirmation, CBCA registered-office certificate, and current Notice of Change of Registered Office filed with the Director, Corporations Canada.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route as SWIFT MT103 from the foreign shareholder's bank to the Canadian account-holding bank, referencing the bank's SWIFT BIC and the Canadian Clearing Code (CC, 8-9 digits comprising 3-digit institution + 5-digit transit). Include payer's full legal name, the CBCA incorporation number, and free-text field 70: 'Share Subscription - [Entity Full Name] - No ECB approval required' to evidence purpose. Banks will initiate a FINTRAC Electronic Funds Transfer Report for the incoming CAD or USD amount if equal to or above CAD 10,000 or equivalent. For USD capital, the transfer may be wired Fedwire or via CHIPS, converted at commercial rate on settlement or held as a USD sub-account. Any foreign investment creating control of the business triggers a simple Investment Canada Act notice within 30 days after implementation; funds are released to the operating account immediately after KYC confirmation without need for escrow release instructions, provided the Capital Escrow Account is used only when joint sign-off is required by non-resident shareholders.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rail hierarchy: (i) domestic CAD payables through Payments Canada ACSS via ACH credits with real-time settlement option on the Lynx system for individual instructions at or above CAD 10,000,000; (ii) US-dollar vendor payments and cloud-infrastructure subscription fees through the bank's USD corridor using SWIFT MT103 with full beneficiary details (send MT103 not MT202 to avoid intermediated-beneficiary ambiguity); (iii) documentary trade for hardware or limited-license procurement from Asia via a confirmed irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit issued by a Schedule I bank, adding a 5-10% CAD/USD cushion for freight and duty discrepancies; (iv) cross-border payroll and contractor remuneration via cross-border ACH into US accounts or SWIFT MT103 into EEA SEPA accounts; (v) Stripe Billing settlement via Stripe's Canadian entity into the D-SIB account through ACSS or the PayPal/Stripe UK EMI corridor when USD pricing is applied. All outbound transfers at or above CAD 10,000 are captured under FINTRAC monitoring and retained in the treasury ledger for Part XIII withholding reconciliation and CRA EBUS reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (1-12 month tenors) under the ISDA 1998 FX Definitions with a Schedule I bank or global derivative dealer, executed without leverage restrictions and settled deliverable CAD/USD.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on CNY, KRW, INR, or other restricted currencies where the CAD or USD leg is settled and the nondeliverable leg is netted in CAD with cash settlement at fixing; no prohibition exists for Canadian corporates.
Rolling-Spot and Window Forwards for converting USD SaaS revenue into CAD payroll during multi-month collection cycles.

Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) for CAD/USD interest and principal exchanges on a one-year facility, admissible with an eligible swap dealer subject to Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA) non-cleared margin rules.
Plain-vanilla FX Options (CAD calls / USD puts and inverse structures) for subscription-revenue downside protection with upfront premium and no ongoing margin.

Structured NDF-Ladder for CNH-denominated rental-screening fees from Asia-Pacific property owners, permissible provided each leg meets commodity-trade substance documentation and the trade is reported under the Canadian Derivatives Act (OSFI) transaction-level rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CBCA Annual Return (confirmation of registered office, directors and beneficial ownership/ISC information)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Director, Corporations Canada - Innovation, Science and Economic Development (ISED) Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing charges may apply; failure to file two consecutive annual returns exposes the corporation to administrative dissolution by the Director under the CBCA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and administered provincial corporate income taxes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the taxation year-end; a December 31 year-end requires filing by June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months, increased repeated-filing penalties, and daily prescribed interest; no administrative strike-off but CRA collection and enforcement remedies apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T4 Statement of Remuneration and T4 Summary (payroll information returns, if employees are engaged)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of February following the calendar year in which remuneration was paid
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per return per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500); uncorrected omissions may attract further fines but do not trigger corporate dissolution.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal corporate income tax (general rate); 9% federal rate for Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPC) on qualified active business income up to CAD 500,000; provincial/territorial corporate rates apply in addition to the federal rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory federal tax holidays. Preferential deductions and credits include the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) Investment Tax Credit (35% refundable for CCPCs up to CAD 3,000,000 of qualifying expenditures; 15% non-refundable/refundable for other corporations), 100% capital cost allowance for certain eligible software under CCA Class 12, and the federal Patent Box / Patent Income Deduction for income derived from qualifying patents where applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically through the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via EFILE, Internet File Transfer, or CRA My Business Account; GIFI financial statement data must be attached.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (one T2 return per fiscal period), with quarterly income tax instalments where estimated Part I tax for the year exceeds CAD 3,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return must be filed no later than six months after the end of the fiscal period; instalments are due on the 15th day of the second, fourth, seventh, and tenth months of the taxation year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the corporation, CRA Business Number (BN), statutory address, and fiscal period end date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers must enter the Canadian branch's legal name and the BN assigned by the CRA for the branch; do not use the foreign parent's BN or address as the primary taxpayer identity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provincial/territorial corporation tax account identifiers and permanent establishment location(s).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate all Canadian provinces/territories in which a permanent establishment is maintained; complete Schedule 5 to allocate taxable income using revenue and payroll factors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax residence status: resident, non-resident, or deemed resident; treaty application indicator if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign-owned Canadian-incorporated SaaS corporation, the entity is resident by incorporation under domestic law; non-resident shareholders should not claim treaty tie-breaker relief unless the central management and control test supports an alternative residence and an applicable income tax treaty is invoked.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report total revenue and detailed Canadian and foreign business income from SaaS subscription fees, tenant screening services, ACH facilitation fees, and platform commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations report only Canadian-source business income attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment; amounts earned without Canadian nexus should be excluded from the T2 unless a permanent establishment exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible business expenses: payroll, cloud infrastructure, development costs, marketing, legal and professional fees, rent, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be reasonably and verifiably allocated to the Canadian permanent establishment; notional head-office recharges or intercompany management fees must satisfy arm’s length principles and transfer-pricing documentation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of investments in Canadian real estate, shares of Canadian subsidiaries, foreign subsidiaries, and taxable Canadian property.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must disclose dispositions of taxable Canadian property; a clearance certificate under Section 116 is required when disposing of such property, forming the basis of a final withholding tax reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of net income plus/minus adjustments, application of non-capital loss carryforwards, allowable capital losses, and SR&ED deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforwards must be computed solely against Canadian taxable income; foreign tax losses cannot be applied to reduce Canadian Part I income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of federal and provincial/territorial Part I tax, application of foreign tax credits and investment tax credits, and final tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations may claim treaty-based foreign tax credits only to the extent Canadian tax is paid on the same income; Part XIII withheld amounts must be reconciled with the T2 liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the unpaid federal/provincial Part I tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months. Gross negligence penalties under Section 163(2) apply at 50% of understated income. Interest accrues at prescribed daily rates. Criminal prosecution under Section 239 can result in fines between 50% and 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, subject to reduction under an applicable bilateral Income Tax Convention to generally 15% for portfolio dividends and 5% for dividends paid to a corporate beneficial owner holding at least 10% of the voting capital.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Canadian payer must withhold the statutory 25% rate on dividend, royalty, and interest payments made to a non-resident unless a valid relief mechanism is in place. The non-resident recipient must supply a certificate of residence issued by its home tax authority (e.g., IRS Form 6166 for a US resident) as well as a completed CRA Form NR301/NR302/NR303 to CRA where applicable. For treaty-reduced withholding, the payer must file an NR4 information return with the CRA within 30 days after the payment date, and the recipient must satisfy any Limitation-on-Benefits (LOB) clause in the treaty, including adequate economic substance in the residence state.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate for interest and royalty income is 25%. Arm’s-length interest paid to a non-resident lender is exempt from Canadian withholding tax provided the loan is genuine, interest-bearing, and not participating debt. Royalties paid under treaty to US or other treaty-resident beneficiaries are commonly reduced to 10%; certain cultural/authorial royalties may be reduced to 0%. Interest paid to treaty residents is generally reduced to 0% under most Canadian DTAs when the beneficial owner is arm's length.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Filing of Form T106 must occur where the aggregate value of non-arm's length transactions with a non-resident exceeds CAD 1,000,000 in a taxation year. Contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation must be prepared and retained when such transactions exist; Country-by-Country (CbC) reporting applies to Canadian ultimate parent entities of multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least CAD 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations, but the Canada Revenue Agency applies the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR), sham doctrine, substance-over-form, and beneficial ownership analysis under treaty LOB provisions. A PropTech real-estate SaaS corporation must maintain real strategic decision-making, employees, office premises, and business purpose in Canada; a shell or conduit with passive receipts and no local substance will face re-characterization, denial of treaty relief, and Part XIII assessments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully omitting Canadian-source SaaS subscription revenue from the T2 return, under-reporting income, claiming false SR&ED expenditures, or using non-arm's length fees to shift profit to offshore entities without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil gross-negligence penalty of 50% of understated tax under ITA s. 163(2); criminal prosecution under ITA s. 239 for tax evasion: upon conviction by indictment, a fine of 50% to 200% of tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years; for summary conviction, a fine up to CAD 10,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years; interest and penalties compound on all arrears.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly participated in the evasion are jointly and severally liable for corporate tax debts under ITA s. 227.1 for unremitted withholdings; criminal liability attaches to those who 'caused, authorized, acquiesced or participated' in the offence; the CRA may obtain asset freezes and garnishments, and a court may prohibit a director from leaving Canada during a serious evasion investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham / Lack of Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Canadian holding or finance entity with no employees, no office, no board meetings, and no real activity beyond intercompany invoicing or dividend traps to access treaty benefits or lower tax rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR re-characterization of the structure, denial of DTA benefits, loss disallowance, and gross-negligence penalty where false statements are made; failure to file T2 returns for two years can lead to administrative dissolution of the federal corporation under CBCA s. 209, with a fine to each director of up to CAD 5,000 and prohibition from acting as director for up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be assessed under ITA s. 227.1 for unremitted Part XIII or source deduction liabilities; CBCA s. 209 exposes directors to personal fines if the corporation is struck off for non-filing; a court can order equitable compensation where the corporate veil is pierced on grounds of sham or fraudulent intention.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's length prices on intercompany SaaS licenses, royalties, management fees, or cost-sharing with non-resident related parties; failing to maintain contemporaneous documentation; executing contracts that do not correspond to actual functions, assets, and risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may re-determine income under ITA s. 247(2); a transfer-pricing penalty of 10% of the net adjustment may apply where the taxpayer has not made reasonable efforts; foreign withholding tax under Part XIII is assessed on any deemed dividend/royalty; interest is charged on the additional tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign inaccurate or fraudulent TP documentation may be subject to gross-negligence penalties and may be personally liable for unremitted amounts; wilful participation in a false transfer-pricing scheme can lead to criminal exposure and personal civil liability for unpaid corporate taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing ACH or tenant-fund flows without a FINTRAC-registered money services business program where applicable; failing to identify beneficial owners, neglecting Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs), or knowingly accepting proceeds from unlawful real-estate or rental fraud on the PropTech platform.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act of up to CAD 1,000,000 per violation for corporations; criminal conviction for knowingly failing to report a transaction can result in imprisonment and fines; FINTRAC may make public enforcement notices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be held personally liable for AML penalties where they knew, caused, consented to, or negligently failed to prevent the offence; criminal sanctions include fines up to CAD 500,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years; CRA may use AML-derived evidence to assess unreported income and impose related tax penalties.
